current.text: The projected starting five is Haliburton, Nembhard, Nesmith, Siakam and Zubac.
If Kelly Oubre Jr. starts, he would take Nesmith's spot.
The projected bench rotation is Oubre as sixth man, then Toppin, Huff, McConnell and Jarace Walker.
Jay Huff is the backup center. Micah Potter is gone.
How Carlisle splits center minutes between Zubac and Huff is a big open question. There may be more experimenting at center than in past years.
Center depth behind Huff is weak: Larry Nance Jr. or Kobe Brown.
Carlisle is expected to manage Haliburton's minutes early in the season.
This lineup loses a lot of shooting but should be better on defense.
Experts expect a good team, with projections of 46 to 48 wins and a top-six seed in the East.
The window with this core may only be one or two years.
Being close to the first apron limited the team's offseason spending.
The fantasy playoff schedule is not ideal for our March 28 end. It has 3, 4 and 3 games in weeks 19 to 21, with a back-to-back in both week 20 and week 21.
The team has 15 back-to-backs and a coach who rests players on them. So IND players carry real rest risk, including in playoff weeks 20 and 21.

durable.text: Coach Rick Carlisle keeps regular-season minutes low and cuts minutes even for healthy players.
Carlisle likes to rest players on back-to-backs.
Carlisle limits his starting center's minutes and runs backup centers through the rotation, as he did with Myles Turner.

note: Rick Carlisle keeps minutes low, so IND starters lose counting stats. Zubac is hit hardest because Carlisle limits his starting centers, which keeps Huff alive as a handcuff, and Haliburton should have his minutes managed early. The playoff schedule is poor (3-4-3 games with two back-to-backs), so watch the Zubac and Huff minutes split, Haliburton's minutes and whether Oubre takes Nesmith's starting spot.
